newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden's Assidoman 9-mo profit on target.
newsitem.headline: Sweden's Assidoman 9-mo profit on target.

text.p: Swedish forestry company AssiDoman reported on Tuesday a nine-month profit exactly in line with analysts' forecasts but more than 50 percent below the figure achieved this time last year.
Hit by lower prices which have also affected the figures of other forestry concerns, Assidoman said its nine-month result after financial items fell 52 percent to 1.62 billion crowns ($246 million).
Assidoman, one of Sweden's most widely held shares, blamed lower prices for many of its products, the stronger Swedish crown and production limitations for the lower profit.
At 1.62 billion crowns, the nine-month figure was spot on target with analysts' forecasts which averaged 1.62 billion crowns in a range of 1.5 to 1.8 billion crowns.
"The lower prices explain for the most part the deterioration of the result," Assidoman, Sweden's largest forestry owner by area, said in a statement.
The stronger crown coupled with the effects of currency hedging weighed the nine-month results to the tune of 400 million crowns, Assidoman said.
It warned that the final quarter of this year would be burdened by a 200 million crown charge ahead of restructuring and job losses in its packaging and Kraft Products divisions.
Forestry and timber sales in the nine months ended September 30 fell 12 percent to 4.05 billion crowns and packaging sales were down by the same percentage at 5.81 billion crowns.
Kraft products, the division responsible for pulp and strong paper production, reported sales 20 percent down at 3.68 billion crowns.
